root_cause.text: In drm/gma500/oaktrail_lvds, the init error path did not distinguish between a borrowed I2C adapter obtained via i2c_get_adapter() and a newly allocated gma_i2c_chan, causing oaktrail_lvds_init() to destroy an already-registered adapter it did not own.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states “The error handling does not separate these cases” and that on late init failure it “will try to deregister and free also an adapter that had previously been registered”; the patch fixes this by initializing `ddc_bus = NULL` and changing cleanup from unconditional `gma_i2c_destroy(to_gma_i2c_chan(connector->ddc));` to `if (!IS_ERR_OR_NULL(ddc_bus)) gma_i2c_destroy(ddc_bus);`, so only adapters allocated during init are destroyed.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit states “The error handling does not separate these cases” and that on late init failure it “will try to deregister and free also an adapter that had previously been registered”; the patch fixes this by initializing `ddc_bus = NULL` and changing cleanup from unconditional `gma_i2c_destroy(to_gma_i2c_chan(connector->ddc));` to `if (!IS_ERR_OR_NULL(ddc_bus)) gma_i2c_destroy(ddc_bus);`, so only adapters allocated during init are destroyed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize `ddc_bus` to NULL in `oaktrail_lvds_init` to avoid unsafe use of an uninitialized pointer.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration for `ddc_bus` in `oaktrail_lvds_init` was changed from an uninitialized `struct gma_i2c_chan *ddc_bus;` to an explicitly initialized null pointer `struct gma_i2c_chan *ddc_bus = NULL;`.
intent_record.how: This ensures `ddc_bus` has a defined value if it is referenced before being assigned a valid channel, preventing use of an indeterminate pointer value and allowing subsequent null checks or fallback logic to behave safely.

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard LVDS error-path I2C cleanup so the DDC bus is destroyed only when it was validly created.
intent_record.what: The unconditional call to gma_i2c_destroy(to_gma_i2c_chan(connector->ddc)) in the error path was replaced with a conditional check on ddc_bus using if (!IS_ERR_OR_NULL(ddc_bus)) before calling gma_i2c_destroy(ddc_bus).
intent_record.how: This changes the cleanup path so the I2C bus is destroyed only when ddc_bus was successfully created and is neither NULL nor an error pointer, preventing invalid cleanup calls during initialization failure handling.

grouping_result.intent: Guard LVDS error-path I2C cleanup so the DDC bus is destroyed only when it was validly created.

consistency_review.core_intent: Make LVDS DDC bus error handling safe by ensuring the bus pointer is initialized and only destroyed if it was successfully created.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the faulty LVDS init error path by initializing the DDC/I2C bus pointer and only destroying it when it was actually created, matching the root cause of unsafe cleanup of a non-owned adapter.

candidates.rationale: This unconditional cleanup destroys connector->ddc on the error path without distinguishing whether it refers to a borrowed adapter from i2c_get_adapter() or an owned gma_i2c_chan, directly causing destruction of an unowned, already-registered adapter.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unconditional error-path cleanup destroys connector->ddc as if it were an owned gma_i2c_chan, but connector->ddc may instead hold a borrowed adapter returned by i2c_get_adapter(). That ownership confusion leads oaktrail_lvds_init() to destroy an already-registered adapter it does not own.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant init and error-handling logic clearly enough to decide. The root cause was failure to distinguish a borrowed adapter from i2c_get_adapter() versus an owned gma_i2c_chan, leading to destruction of an adapter not owned by this code. In this commit, the code tracks the adapter source differently: it first does `i2c_adap = i2c_get_adapter(dev_priv->ops->i2c_bus);` and only if EDID is still missing does it call `ddc_bus = oaktrail_lvds_i2c_init(dev);` and, on success, set `i2c_adap = &ddc_bus->base;`. Crucially, the old vulnerable cleanup based on `gma_encoder->ddc_bus` is gone. The removed code was `if (gma_encoder->ddc_bus) { gma_i2c_destroy(gma_encoder->ddc_bus); gma_encoder->ddc_bus = NULL; }`, which could not distinguish ownership correctly. In the new code, `connector->ddc = i2c_adap;` is assigned after probing, and the cleanup path does `gma_i2c_destroy(to_gma_i2c_chan(connector->ddc));`. Given the commit message explicitly says it cleans up the error handling and moves DDC ownership handling, and the old ambiguous `gma_encoder->ddc_bus` path is removed, this function version already reflects the fix rather than the vulnerable construct.
